claims.label: Just Compensation Valuation
claims.note: Severance/access/business-value disputes ran 2x-5x+ above the initial offer in the research sample (one case ~49x).

outcome.description: After a five-day August 2017 trial the Wood County jury awarded $2,000 for the take, $1,800 for the temporary construction easements, and condemnation-blight damages of $35,033 a year for five years (2003-2007), $175,165, for $178,965 in total before interest (against the $3,550 deposit, the $17,500 commissioners' award and Michael Pifer's $812,000 blight claim). The trial court's judgment added 10% pre-petition and post-petition interest for a total of $466,114. The Supreme Court of Appeals affirmed the blight award on November 19, 2019, but reversed the interest calculation and remanded for it to be recomputed under W. Va. Code 54-2-14a.
outcome.finalNote: Principal affirmed ($178,965, the sum of the three verdict items; the opinion never states it as one figure); only the interest computation was reversed and remanded, so the $466,114 judgment total will change.

source.caseName: West Virginia Department of Transportation, Division of Highways v. Lawrence W. Pifer and Michael E. Pifer
source.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia, on appeal from the Circuit Court of Wood County (Civil Action No. 10-C-95)
source.excerptNote: Verbatim from the introduction's description of the owners and project history (without its sentences on the verdict and interest) and Part I, Factual and Procedural History, through the experts' testimony and the jury instruction: the 1998 plan, the 2001 schedule letter, the 2008 plan change, the partial taking, the $3,550 deposit, the $17,500 commissioners' award, the blight claim and DOH's motions in limine, the owners' appraiser's figures ($2,000 take, zero residue damage, $35,000 a year lost rent), Michael Pifer's $812,000 claim, and DOH's appraiser. Removed: the syllabus, the introduction's verdict and $466,114 sentences, footnotes and markers, the jury's awards for the take, easements and blight, the judgment and post-trial motion, and all of the discussion and holdings.
